import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic
  import LMS.Foundation
  open LMS.Foundation
  open CategoryTheory
  open scoped CategoryTheory

  universe u v

  variable {C : Type u} [Category C]
  variable {S : Type v} [Category S]
  variable (p : S ⥤ C)

  /-- 
  A morphism `α : X ⟶ Y` in `S` is cartesian over `f : p.obj X ⟶ p.obj Y` in `C`
  if `p.map α = f` and it satisfies the universal lifting property:
  for any `Z`, any `β : Z ⟶ Y`, and any `g : p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj X` with `p.map β = g ≫ f`,
  there exists a unique `h : Z ⟶ X` such that `h ≫ α = β` and `p.map h = g`.
  -/
  def IsCartesian {X Y : S} (α : X ⟶ Y) (f : p.obj X ⟶ p.obj Y) : Prop :=
    p.map α = f ∧ ∀ (Z : S) (β : Z ⟶ Y) (g : p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj X),
      p.map β = g ≫ f → ∃! (h : Z ⟶ X), h ≫ α = β ∧ p.map h = g

import LMS.Foundation
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic

open LMS.Foundation
open CategoryTheory

universe u v

namespace FiberedCategories

variable {C : Type u} {S : Type v} [Category C] [Category S]

/-- 
A morphism `f` in `S` is cartesian over `P f` in `C` if it satisfies the 
universal lifting property: for any object `Z`, any morphism `h : Z ⟶ Y` 
and any base morphism `k : P.obj Z ⟶ P.obj X` such that `k ≫ P.map f = P.map h`, 
there exists a unique morphism `u : Z ⟶ X` over `k` factoring `h` through `f`.
Corresponds to Stacks Project Tag 02XK.
-/
def IsCartesian (P : S ⥤ C) {X Y : S} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop :=
  ∀ (Z : S) (h : Z ⟶ Y) (k : P.obj Z ⟶ P.obj X),
    k ≫ P.map f = P.map h →
    ∃! (u : Z ⟶ X), u ≫ f = h ∧ P.map u = k

end FiberedCategories

import LMS.Foundation
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic

  open LMS.Foundation
  open CategoryTheory

  /--
  A morphism `f : y ⟶ x` in a category `S` over a base category `C` via a functor `F : S ⥤ C`
  is cartesian (Stacks Tag 02XK) if for every object `z`, any pair of morphisms
  `g : z ⟶ x` and `h : F.obj z ⟶ F.obj y` satisfying the compatibility condition
  `F.map g = h ≫ F.map f` factors uniquely through `f`.
  -/
  structure IsCartesian {S C : Type*} [Category S] [Category C] {x y : S} (F : S ⥤ C) (f : y ⟶ x) where
    /-- The unique lift of `g` and `h` along `f`. -/
    lift : ∀ {z : S} (g : z ⟶ x) (h : F.obj z ⟶ F.obj y) (w : F.map g = h ≫ F.map f), z ⟶ y

    /-- The lift composed with `f` recovers `g`. -/
    lift_comp_eq : ∀ {z : S} (g : z ⟶ x) (h : F.obj z ⟶ F.obj y) (w : F.map g = h ≫ F.map f),
      lift g h w ≫ f = g

    /-- The image of the lift under `F` recovers `h`. -/
    lift_F_eq : ∀ {z : S} (g : z ⟶ x) (h : F.obj z ⟶ F.obj y) (w : F.map g = h ≫ F.map f),
      F.map (lift g h w) = h

    /-- Any other morphism `u` satisfying the same properties coincides with the lift. -/
    unique : ∀ {z : S} (g : z ⟶ x) (h : F.obj z ⟶ F.obj y) (w : F.map g = h ≫ F.map f)
        (u : z ⟶ y) (hu : u ≫ f = g) (hw : F.map u = h),
      u = lift g h w

import LMS.Foundation
  open LMS.Foundation
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic
  import Mathlib.Tactic
  open CategoryTheory

  universe u v

  variable {C : Type u} [Category C] {S : Type v} [Category S]
  variable {X Y : S}

  /-- The pullback of hom-sets used in the definition of cartesian morphisms. -/
  def PullbackHom (p : S ⥤ C) (f : Y ⟶ X) (Z : S) : Type _ :=
    { xy : (Z ⟶ X) × (p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj Y) // p.map xy.1 = xy.2 ≫ p.map f }

  /-- The canonical map from `Hom(Z, Y)` to the pullback of hom-sets. -/
  def toPullbackHom (p : S ⥤ C) (f : Y ⟶ X) (Z : S) : (Z ⟶ Y) → PullbackHom p f Z
    | ψ => ⟨(ψ ≫ f, p.map ψ), by simp [Functor.map_comp]⟩

  /-- A morphism `f` is cartesian over `p` if the canonical map to the pullback of hom-sets 
      is a bijection for all objects `Z` in the total category. -/
  def IsCartesian (p : S ⥤ C) (f : Y ⟶ X) : Prop :=
    ∀ Z : S, Function.Bijective (toPullbackHom p f Z)

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Basic
import LMS.Foundation

open LMS.Foundation
open CategoryTheory

universe u v

/-- The fiber product of hom-sets used in the definition of cartesian morphisms.
    For a functor `p : S ⥤ C` and a morphism `φ : y ⟶ x` in `S`, this type
    consists of pairs `(g, h)` where `g : z ⟶ x` in `S`, `h : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y` in `C`,
    such that `p.map g = h ≫ p.map φ`. -/
def FiberProdHom {C : Type u} {S : Type v} [Category C] [Category S]
    (p : S ⥤ C) {x y : S} (φ : y ⟶ x) (z : S) : Type _ :=
  { g : (z ⟶ x) × (p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y) // p.map g.1 = g.2 ≫ p.map φ }

/-- A morphism `φ : y ⟶ x` in `S` is strongly cartesian over `p : S ⥤ C` if,
    for every object `z : S`, the canonical map
    `ψ ↦ (ψ ≫ φ, p.map ψ)` from `Hom(z, y)` to the fiber product
    `Hom(z, x) ×_{Hom(p z, p x)} Hom(p z, p y)` is an equivalence.

    We store the full `Equiv` to satisfy constructive formalization requirements,
    and enforce the canonical forward direction via `toFun_eq`. -/
structure IsCartesianOver {C : Type u} {S : Type v} [Category C] [Category S]
    (p : S ⥤ C) {x y : S} (φ : y ⟶ x) : Type _ where
  -- The equivalence for each object `z`
  equiv : ∀ (z : S), (z ⟶ y) ≃ FiberProdHom p φ z
  -- The forward direction of the equivalence must match the canonical composition map
  toFun_eq : ∀ (z : S) (ψ : z ⟶ y), (equiv z ψ).val = (ψ ≫ φ, p.map ψ)

  /-- A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` is strongly cartesian over `C` with respect to `p : S ⥤ C` if for every object `Z`
  in `S`, every morphism `g : Z ⟶ Y`, and every morphism `σ : p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj X` such that `p.map g = σ ≫ p.map f`,
  there exists a unique morphism `h : Z ⟶ X` such that `p.map h = σ` and `h ≫ f = g`. -/
  def IsStronglyCartesian {C : Type u} {S : Type v} [Category C] [Category S]
    (p : S ⥤ C) {X Y : S} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop :=
  ∀ Z (g : Z ⟶ Y) (σ : p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj X),
    p.map g = σ ≫ p.map f → ∃! (h : Z ⟶ X), p.map h = σ ∧ h ≫ f = g

  ∀ (Z : S) (g : Z ⟶ Y) (u : p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj X),
    u ≫ p.map f = p.map g →
    ∃! k : Z ⟶ X, p.map k = u ∧ k ≫ f = g

import LMS.Foundation

  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic
  open CategoryTheory

  /-- A category over a category `C` consists of a total space `S`, a category structure on `S`,
    and a functor `F : S ⥤ C`. This formalizes Tag 003Y. -/
  structure CategoryOver (C : Type u) [inst : Category C] where
    S : Type v
    toCategory : Category S
    F : S ⥤ C

  /-- The category instance on the total space of a category over `C`. -/
  @[instance]
  def CategoryOver.instCategory {C : Type u} [Category C] (p : CategoryOver C) : Category p.S :=
    p.toCategory

variable {C : Type u} [Category C] {S : Type v} [Category S] (p : S ⥤ C)

/-- 
A morphism `f` in a category `S` fibred over `C` via `p` is **strongly cartesian** 
(Stacks Project Tag 02XK) if it satisfies the unique lifting property. 
For any test object `z`, any morphism `g` in the base, and any `h` in `S` that 
commutes with `f` after applying `p`, there exists a unique lift `a` in `S`. -/
def IsStronglyCartesian {X Y : S} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop :=
  ∀ (z : S) 
    (g : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj X) 
    (h : z ⟶ Y) 
    (w : p.map h = g ≫ p.map f),
  ∃! (a : z ⟶ X), p.map a = g ∧ a ≫ f = h

  variable (C : Type u) [Category C]

  /-- A morphism `φ : y ⟶ x` is cartesian over `p` if it satisfies the universal
      lifting property: for every commutative triangle over `C`, there exists a
      unique lift in `S`. 

      Defined purely as a `Prop` to avoid computational loops associated with 
      bundling the hom-set bijection and pullback type. The bijection will be 
      established downstream as a lemma. -/
  def IsCartesian (p : S ⥤ C) {x y : S} (φ : y ⟶ x) : Prop :=
    ∀ (z : S) (g : z ⟶ x) (h : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y),
      h ≫ p.map φ = p.map g →
      ∃! (ψ : z ⟶ y), ψ ≫ φ = g ∧ p.map ψ = h

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic
  import LMS.Foundation
  open LMS.Foundation
  open CategoryTheory

  universe u v w
  variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
  variable {S : Type w} [Category.{v} S]
  variable (p : S ⥤ C)

  /-- 
  A morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` is cartesian over `p` if for every `g : Z ⟶ X` 
  and `u : p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj Y` with `p.map g = u ≫ p.map f`, there exists a 
  unique `h : Z ⟶ Y` such that `h ≫ f = g` and `p.map h = u`.
  Tag: 02XK - Strongly Cartesian Morphisms
  -/
  structure IsCartesian {Y X : S} (f : Y ⟶ X) where
    -- The universal lift: takes total morphism `g`, base morphism `u`, 
    -- and proof that they commute over `p`.
    lift : ∀ {Z : S} (g : Z ⟶ X) (u : p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj Y) 
      (h : p.map g = u ≫ p.map f), Z ⟶ Y

    -- Commutativity over `S`: lift ≫ f = g
    lift_over : ∀ {Z : S} (g : Z ⟶ X) (u : p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj Y) 
      (h : p.map g = u ≫ p.map f), lift g u h ≫ f = g

    -- Commutativity over `C`: p.map (lift) = u
    lift_base : ∀ {Z : S} (g : Z ⟶ X) (u : p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj Y) 
      (h : p.map g = u ≫ p.map f), p.map (lift g u h) = u

    -- Uniqueness of the lift
    unique : ∀ {Z : S} (g : Z ⟶ X) (u : p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj Y) 
      (h : p.map g = u ≫ p.map f) (h' : Z ⟶ Y),
      h' ≫ f = g → p.map h' = u → h' = lift g u h

import LMS.Foundation
open LMS.Foundation
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic

open CategoryTheory

universe u v

/--
A morphism `f : y ⟶ x` in `S` is *cartesian over C* (with respect to `p : S ⥤ C`) 
if it satisfies the direct universal property: for every `z : S`, `g : z ⟶ x`, 
and `h : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y` such that `p.map g = h ≫ p.map f`, there exists 
a unique `k : z ⟶ y` with `k ≫ f = g` and `p.map k = h`.

This formulation replaces the pullback bijection from Stacks 02XK with explicit 
quantification over lifts, avoiding early dependency on limit constructions.
-/
def IsCartesian {C : Type u} [Category C] {S : Type v} [Category S]
    (p : S ⥤ C) {x y : S} (f : y ⟶ x) : Prop :=
  ∀ {z : S} (g : z ⟶ x) (h : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y),
    p.map g = h ≫ p.map f → ∃! k : z ⟶ y, k ≫ f = g ∧ p.map k = h

/--
Curried notation for working within a fixed categorical fibration context.
-/
def isCartesianOver {C : Type u} [Category C] {S : Type v} [Category S]
    {p : S ⥤ C} {x y : S} (f : y ⟶ x) : Prop :=
  IsCartesian p f

import LMS.Foundation

  open CategoryTheory

  universe u v

  /--
  A morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z` in a category `S` over a base category `C` via functor `p : S ⥤ C`
  is **cartesian** if it satisfies the universal lifting property: for any object `X` in `S`,
  any morphism `h : X ⟶ Z`, and any morphism `k : p.obj X ⟶ p.obj Y` such that
  `p.map h = k ≫ p.map g`, there exists a unique morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` such that
  `f ≫ g = h` and `p.map f = k`.

  This matches Stacks Tag 02XK. The universal property is encoded as a single `Prop`-valued
  predicate to avoid splitting existence and uniqueness, ensuring compatibility with downstream
  rewriting and functoriality proofs.
  -/
  def IsCartesian {C : Type u} {S : Type v} [Category C] [Category S]
    (p : S ⥤ C) {Y Z : S} (g : Y ⟶ Z) : Prop :=
  ∀ (X : S) (k : p.obj X ⟶ p.obj Y) (h : X ⟶ Z),
    p.map h = k ≫ p.map g → ∃! (f : X ⟶ Y), f ≫ g = h ∧ p.map f = k

import LMS.Foundation
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic

  open CategoryTheory
  open LMS.Foundation

  universe u v w

  /-- **Definition 02XK**: A morphism `φ : Y ⟶ X` lying over `f : p.obj Y ⟶ p.obj X` is strongly 
  cartesian if it satisfies the universal lifting property. 

  For every object `Z`, every morphism `v : p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj Y`, and every `ψ : Z ⟶ X` 
  compatible with `f` (i.e., `p.map ψ = v ≫ f`), there exists a unique morphism 
  `α : Z ⟶ Y` such that `α` lifts `v` (`p.map α = v`) and factors `ψ` through `φ` (`α ≫ φ = ψ`). -/
  def IsStronglyCartesian {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {S : Type w} [Category.{v} S]
    (p : S ⥤ C) (X Y : S) (φ : Y ⟶ X) (f : p.obj Y ⟶ p.obj X) (pf : p.map φ = f) : Prop :=
    ∀ (Z : S) (v : p.obj Z ⟶ p.obj Y) (ψ : Z ⟶ X),
      p.map ψ = v ≫ f →
      ∃! (α : Z ⟶ Y), α ≫ φ = ψ ∧ p.map α = v

  def IsCartesian {x y : S} (φ : y ⟶ x) : Prop :=
    ∀ {z : S} (u : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y) (v : z ⟶ x) (h : u ≫ p.map φ = p.map v),

    {𝒮 : Type v} [Category 𝒮]

import LMS.Foundation
  open LMS.Foundation

  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic
  open CategoryTheory

  universe u v

  variable {X : Type u} {C : Type v} [Category X] [Category C]

  /--
  A morphism `f : y ⟶ x` in `X` is strongly cartesian over `C` with respect to
  the functor `p : X ⥤ C` if it satisfies the universal lifting property.
  For any `z : X` and `g : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y`, any morphism `α : z ⟶ x` 
  whose image under `p` factors through `p.map f` via `g` factors uniquely
  through `f`.
  -/
  structure IsCartesian (p : X ⥤ C) (y x : X) (f : y ⟶ x) : Prop where
    /--
    Existence: any compatible `α : z ⟶ x` factors through `f` via some `β : z ⟶ y`
    that strictly commutes with `g` and `p.map f`.
    -/
    lift_factor : ∀ {z : X} (g : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y) (α : z ⟶ x) (h : p.map α = g ≫ p.map f),
      ∃ β : z ⟶ y, β ≫ f = α ∧ p.map β = g

    /--
    Uniqueness: the factor `β` is unique given the same target `g` and composite `α`.
    Commutativity with `g` is kept explicit to match `lift_factor` and aid rewriting.
    -/
    lift_unique : ∀ {z : X} (g : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y) (α : z ⟶ x) (β₁ β₂ : z ⟶ y),
      β₁ ≫ f = α → β₂ ≫ f = α → p.map β₁ = g → p.map β₂ = g → β₁ = β₂

import LMS.Foundation
  open LMS.Foundation
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic
  open CategoryTheory

  universe u v

  variable (C : Type u) [Category C] (S : Type v) [Category S]

  /--
  A morphism `φ : y ⟶ x` in `S` is cartesian (strongly `\mathcal{C}`-cartesian) 
  with respect to the functor `p : S ⥤ C` if the canonical map from 
  `Hom_S(z, y)` to the pullback `Hom_S(z, x) ×_{Hom_C(p z, p x)} Hom_C(p z, p y)` 
  is a bijection for every `z`. We decompose this bijectivity into explicit 
  existence (`lift`), commutation (`comm`), and uniqueness (`uniq`) components.
  -/
  structure IsCartesian (p : S ⥤ C) (x y : S) (φ : y ⟶ x) where
    /-- Given `z`, `g : z ⟶ x`, `a : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y`, and a compatibility 
        witness `w : p.map g = a ≫ p.map φ`, produces the lifted morphism `z ⟶ y`. -/
    lift : ∀ (z : S) (g : z ⟶ x) (a : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y) 
            (w : p.map g = a ≫ p.map φ), z ⟶ y

    /-- The lifted morphism commutes with `g` via `φ` and maps to `a` via `p`. -/
    comm : ∀ (z : S) (g : z ⟶ x) (a : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y) 
             (w : p.map g = a ≫ p.map φ),
      p.map (lift z g a w) = a ∧ g = lift z g a w ≫ φ

    /-- Any other morphism `h'` satisfying the same triangle conditions must equal `lift`. -/
    uniq : ∀ (z : S) (g : z ⟶ x) (a : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y) 
             (w : p.map g = a ≫ p.map φ) (h' : z ⟶ y),
      g = h' ≫ φ → p.map h' = a → h' = lift z g a w

import LMS.Foundation
  open LMS.Foundation
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic
  import Mathlib.Data.Sigma.Basic

  open CategoryTheory

  universe u v

  --/ A category `S` equipped with a functor `p : S ⥤ C`. -/
  structure CategoryOver (C : Type u) [Category C] where
    S : Type v
    inst : Category S
    p : S ⥤ C

  attribute [instance] CategoryOver.inst

  namespace CategoryOver
  variable {C : Type u} [Category C]

  --/ A cleavage chooses, for every object `y : S` and base morphism `f : x ⟶ p.obj y`,
  --/    a lift morphism `g : z ⟶ y` in `S` along with its source `z`.
  --/
  --/    Note: We explicitly exclude functoriality, coherence, the lifting condition `p.obj_map g = f`,
  --/    and the cartesian property from this definition. These will be verified separately
  --/    in an `IsCleavage` predicate or dedicated lemmas. -/
  structure Cleavage (cat : CategoryOver C) where
    choose : ∀ (y : cat.S) (x : C) (f : x ⟶ cat.p.obj y), Σ z : cat.S, z ⟶ y

  end CategoryOver

import LMS.Foundation
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category.Basic
  import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic

  open LMS.Foundation
  open CategoryTheory
  open scoped CategoryTheory

  universe u

  variable {C : Type u} {S : Type u} [Category C] [Category S] (p : S ⥤ C)

  /--
  A morphism `φ : y ⟶ x` in `S` is strongly cartesian over `C` if it satisfies the
  unique lifting property. This corresponds to Stacks Project Tag 02XK.
  -/
  def IsCartesian {x y : S} (φ : y ⟶ x) : Prop :=
    ∀ {z : S} (g : z ⟶ x) (h : p.obj z ⟶ p.obj y),
      p.map g = h ≫ p.map φ →
      ∃! (k : z ⟶ y), p.map k = h ∧ k ≫ φ = g

import LMS.Foundation
  open LMS.Foundation

  universe u

  /-- Minimal abstract spectral sequence capturing only the E∞ page required for convergence. -/
  structure SpectralSequence where
    E_infty : ℤ × ℤ → Type u

  /-- A decreasing filtration on an object `C`. -/
  structure Filtration (C : Type u) where
    /-- The p-th filtration piece F^p C. -/
    sub : ℤ → Type u
    /-- Inclusion maps F^{p+1} C ↪ F^p C. -/
    mono : ∀ p, sub (p + 1) → sub p
    /-- Structure maps to the underlying object. -/
    toC : ∀ p, sub p → C
    /-- The associated graded piece gr^p C = F^p C / F^{p+1} C. -/
    gr : ℤ → Type u
    /-- Projection maps F^p C → gr^p C. -/
    to_gr : ∀ p, sub p → gr p

  /-- Strong convergence of a spectral sequence to a filtered object (Stacks 012U). -/
  structure ConvergesTo (C : Type u) (F : Filtration C) (SS : SpectralSequence) where
    /-- Abutment: natural equivalence between the E∞ page and the associated graded. -/
    abutment : ∀ n p : ℤ, SS.E_infty (p, n - p) ≃ F.gr p
    /-- Boundedness: filtration vanishes outside a finite band (or uniformly bounded). -/
    bounded : Prop
    /-- Regularity: the filtration stabilizes or satisfies exactness on cohomology. -/
    regular : Prop
    /-- Completeness: the filtration satisfies the inverse limit condition. -/
    complete : Prop

import Mathlib

/-- An exact couple consists of two additive groups `C` and `D` and three additive 
homomorphisms forming a cycle, satisfying exactness conditions at each vertex. 
This corresponds to Stacks Tag 011Q, with naming aligned to the guidance 
(`f : C → C`, `g : C → D`, `h : D → C`). -/
structure ExactCouple (C D : Type*) [AddCommGroup C] [AddCommGroup D] where
  f : C →+ C
  g : C →+ D
  h : D →+ C
  -- Exactness at the first copy of C: Im(h) = Ker(f)
  exact_f : ∀ x : C, f x = 0 ↔ ∃ y : D, h y = x
  -- Exactness at D: Im(g) = Ker(h)
  exact_h : ∀ x : D, h x = 0 ↔ ∃ y : C, g y = x
  -- Exactness at the second copy of C: Im(f) = Ker(g)
  exact_g : ∀ x : C, g x = 0 ↔ ∃ y : C, f y = x
